The UK [Prime Minister](Prime_Minister_of_the_United_Kingdom "Prime Minister of the United Kingdom")'s website has used the phrase "countries within a country" to describe the United Kingdom.[[9]](Countries_of_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-9) Some statistical summaries, such as those for the twelve [NUTS 1 regions of the UK](International_Territorial_Level "International Territorial Level"), refer to Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales as "regions".[[10]](Countries_of_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-10)[[11]](Countries_of_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-11) With regard to Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales particularly, the descriptive name one uses "can be controversial, with the choice often revealing one's political preferences".[[12]](Countries_of_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-12)

Although the United Kingdom is a [unitary](Unitary_state "Unitary state") [sovereign country](Sovereign_state "Sovereign state"), it contains three distinct legal jusridictions in [Scotland](Scots_Law "Scots Law"), [England and Wales](English_Law "English Law"), and [Northern Ireland](Northern_Irish_Law "Northern Irish Law"), each retaining its own legal system even after joining the UK.[[13]](Countries_of_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-13) Since 1998, Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales have also gained significant autonomy through the process of [devolution](Devolution_in_the_United_Kingdom "Devolution in the United Kingdom"). The [United Kingdom Parliament](Parliament_of_the_United_Kingdom "Parliament of the United Kingdom") and [British Government](Government_of_the_United_Kingdom "Government of the United Kingdom") deal with all *[reserved matters](Devolved%2C_reserved_and_excepted_matters "Devolved, reserved and excepted matters")* for Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales, but not in general matters that have been [devolved](Devolution "Devolution") to the [Northern Ireland Assembly](Northern_Ireland_Assembly "Northern Ireland Assembly"), [Scottish Parliament](Scottish_Parliament "Scottish Parliament"), and the Welsh <Senedd>. Additionally, devolution in Northern Ireland is conditional on co-operation between the [Northern Ireland Executive](Northern_Ireland_Executive "Northern Ireland Executive") and the [Government of Ireland](Government_of_Ireland "Government of Ireland") (see [North/South Ministerial Council](North/South_Ministerial_Council "North/South Ministerial Council")) and the British Government consults with the Government of Ireland to reach agreement on some non-devolved matters for Northern Ireland (see [British–Irish Intergovernmental Conference](British%E2%80%93Irish_Intergovernmental_Conference "British–Irish Intergovernmental Conference")). England, comprising the majority of the population and area of the United Kingdom,[[14]](Countries_of_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-14)[[15]](Countries_of_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-ONSCOUNTRYPROFILES-15) remains fully the responsibility of the United Kingdom Parliament centralised in <London>.

However the ISO list of the subdivisions of the United Kingdom, compiled by [British Standards](British_Standards "British Standards") and the United Kingdom's [Office for National Statistics](Office_for_National_Statistics "Office for National Statistics"), uses "country" to describe England, Scotland, and Wales.[[16]](Countries_of_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-ISO_Newsletter_ii-3-2011-12-13-16) Northern Ireland, in contrast, is described as a "province" in the same lists.[[16]](Countries_of_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-ISO_Newsletter_ii-3-2011-12-13-16) Each has separate [national governing bodies for sports](Sport_governing_body "Sport governing body") and compete separately in many international sporting competitions, including the [Commonwealth Games](Commonwealth_Games "Commonwealth Games"). Northern Ireland also forms joint [All-Island](Island_of_Ireland "Island of Ireland") sporting bodies with the [Republic of Ireland](Republic_of_Ireland "Republic of Ireland") for some sports, including [rugby union](Rugby_union "Rugby union").[[17]](Countries_of_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-17)

The [Channel Islands](Channel_Islands "Channel Islands") and the [Isle of Man](Isle_of_Man "Isle of Man") are [dependencies](Crown_Dependencies "Crown Dependencies") of [the Crown](The_Crown "The Crown") and are not part of the UK. Similarly, the [British Overseas Territories](British_Overseas_Territories "British Overseas Territories"), remnants of the [British Empire](British_Empire "British Empire"), are not part of the UK.

From 1801, following the [Acts of Union](Acts_of_Union_1800 "Acts of Union 1800"), until 1922 the whole island of <Ireland> was a country within the UK. Ireland was [split into two separate jurisdictions](Government_of_Ireland_Act_1920 "Government of Ireland Act 1920") in 1921, becoming [Southern Ireland](Southern_Ireland_(1921%E2%80%9322) "Southern Ireland (1921–22)") and [Northern Ireland](Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland"). Pursuant to the [Anglo-Irish Treaty](Anglo-Irish_Treaty "Anglo-Irish Treaty"), the institutions of the [revolutionary Irish Republic](Irish_Republic "Irish Republic") were assimilated into Southern Ireland, which then became the [Irish Free State](Irish_Free_State "Irish Free State") and left the United Kingdom in 1922. The Irish Free State adopted a new, essentially republican [constitution](Constitution_of_Ireland "Constitution of Ireland") in 1937 – albeit [retaining the King for diplomatic functions](Irish_head_of_state_from_1922_to_1949#Ambiguity_from_1936_to_1949 "Irish head of state from 1922 to 1949") – by which it would be known as simply Ireland. In 1949, by the [Republic of Ireland Act](Republic_of_Ireland_Act "Republic of Ireland Act"), it transferred these diplomatic functions to [its own president](President_of_Ireland "President of Ireland"), left the [Commonwealth of Nations](British_Commonwealth "British Commonwealth") and adopted the description [Republic of Ireland](Republic_of_Ireland "Republic of Ireland"), by which it is now known.
